title: EXP-133 — Minimal FX_LoginPortal With Client Validation and Form Script Bridge
objective: Create exactly one User-scoped Classic BuildFromScratch Form named FX_LoginPortal, two associated Web User Control assets, one Global persistent variable, one UserControl component and one C# Form Script method. The login interface will validate input locally and, for a valid fake test pair, invoke FX_ProcessLogin and display the nonsensitive code received through WSForm.getVarValue. Complete one ordinary Designer Save, one close/reopen with readback, and one controlled runtime submission. Establish observable behavior and same-session definition retention without claiming real authentication, definitive Global-variable resolution, independent database durability or replay verification.

in_scope: Read AGENTS.md, EXP-130 T5 sections 13–16 and plan steps P5/P6, EXP-131, EXP-132, recipes/forms/create-basic-form.md and the relevant Web User Control guidance before browser mutation.

Perform the EXP-132 account gate: authenticated header anton.ramos@3mworks.com.ph, configuration G6R8LJ9Q4E8C2Z8Y_MONGOOSE_DEM_DEFAULT, editing scope User, FX_CustomerPortal visible as a positive control, and no visible scoped matches for MockLoginPortal or FX_InventoryPrototype01. Never open either excluded Form. Treat scoped inventory evidence as distinct from tenant-wide absence.

Verify FX_LoginPortal is absent from the applicable Form inventory, and FX_Login/index.html, FX_Login/script/app.js and FX_vLoginResult are absent from the corresponding supported asset and variable inventories. Record exact-name and case-insensitive findings where the supported UI permits. Stop rather than overwrite any existing definition.

Create one User-scoped Form FX_LoginPortal through the verified Classic BuildFromScratch Form recipe, with Save Template unchecked and Script Language Visual C#. The first creation may involve the wizard's own persistence operation; distinguish it from the experiment's single later ordinary Designer Form Save.
Create exactly two Web User Control assets: FX_Login/index.html and FX_Login/script/app.js. No third asset or stylesheet.

Configure FX_Login/index.html to load ../$app/scripts/UserControl.js as an unchanged dependency and script/app.js as the FX_-owned application script. Render a minimal login card with one username input, one password input of type password, one Sign in button and one result element with ID FX_LoginResult. Minimal inline styling is permitted.

Implement FX_Login/script/app.js so client validation requires a trimmed username of at least three characters and a password of at least six characters. A validation failure displays a nonsensitive message in FX_LoginResult and returns without invoking the server method. Valid input invokes FX_ProcessLogin with the username and password through the documented WSForm.invoke argument pattern. Its completion callback calls WSForm.getVarValue for FX_vLoginResult and writes the returned value to FX_LoginResult. Confirm the two-argument invocation pattern against the approved source guidance before committing it; stop for operator review if the signature cannot be established.

Create exactly one Global persistent variable FX_vLoginResult through the EXP-132 Edit > Variable > Global Objects > New route. Verify Name, Global=True, Persistent=True, initially blank Value and the operator's User version. Do not create a second variable if its visibility is delayed.

Place exactly one UserControl component FX_LoginControl on FX_LoginPortal. Name it before the first ordinary Designer Save where supported. Configure Use Web Control and Control URL FX_Login/index.html. Inventory any Mongoose-generated UserCtrl variables and prevent duplicate or stale definitions; do not manually create or alter non-FX variables. Stop for operator disposition if a newly generated non-FX artifact would violate the FX_ boundary.

Implement one public string FX_ProcessLogin(string username, string password) method within FX_LoginPortal's Visual C# Form Script. Set ThisForm.Variables("FX_vLoginResult").Value to one nonsensitive literal code: missing when either argument is null, empty when either argument is blank after trimming, and received otherwise. Return precisely the same code. Do not persist or expose either input argument.

Capture source and properties before committing. After all approved definition changes, perform exactly one ordinary Designer Form Save and verify the saved notification or supported result, Save disabled, and no unexpected dialog or new console errors.

Close FX_LoginPortal once through the ordinary Designer Form-tab close control and reopen it once through the supported recent-forms path. Read back the User-scoped Form identity, Visual C# method, both assets, FX_vLoginResult properties, FX_LoginControl reference and any generated variables. Leave the definition unchanged and Save disabled.

Open the runtime FX_LoginPortal Form once. Enter only the fixed fake test username fx_probe and password fx-probe-only. Activate Sign in exactly once. Capture the displayed FX_LoginResult value and verify received is visible with no alert, no unmasked password and no new console errors. Close the runtime Form once without saving.

Write decisive screenshots and concise source/readback summaries under evidence/EXP-133/. Record the complete Mongoose object inventory, action counts, console changes, recovery usage, created files, deviations and limitations. Update only the EXP-133 experiment record and its evidence directory.
out_of_scope: Real authentication, user lookup, credential verification, sessions, authorization, cookies or authentication tokens.
Any IDO, SQL table, database record, API endpoint or external system.
Recreating MockLoginPortal's Flex Form structure; this experiment deliberately uses Classic BuildFromScratch.
Additional login pages, navigation, dashboards, routing, styling frameworks, CSS asset files or responsive-layout reconstruction.
Runtime tests with real credentials or additional credential combinations.
Modifications to any Mock object, FX_InventoryPrototype01, FX_CustomerPortal, shared $app assets, or the EXP-131/EXP-132 bridge artifacts.
Investigating whether the Global FX_vLoginResult definition is the storage actually resolved by ThisForm.Variables and WSForm.getVarValue.
Proving server-side credential security, independent compilation success, database durability, cross-session persistence or replay verification.
Promoting a verified recipe or altering existing recipes, AGENTS.md or environment configuration.

prohibited_actions: Creating, modifying or deleting any non-FX_ artifact
Starting any other experiment or replay
Modifying production data or disabling security
Reading or printing credential values
Do not open, edit, delete, rename, save or regenerate FX_InventoryPrototype01 or any Mock object.
Do not change FX_BridgeTest, FX_BridgeControl, FX_Echo, FX_Bridge/index.html, FX_vEcho, FX_CustomerPortal or their existing generated variables.
Do not modify, overwrite or upload the shared $app/scripts/UserControl.js asset; reference it only as an unchanged dependency.
Do not create or modify IDOs, tables, property classes, validators, database records or any Global Object other than FX_vLoginResult.
Do not create additional Form Script methods, event handlers or components outside the specified FX_LoginPortal inventory.
Do not use genuine credentials. Do not persist, log, echo, alert, display, return or include either username or password in the FX_vLoginResult value or method result.
Do not save or expose a clear-text password in screenshots, browser logs, repository files or evidence. Keep the password input masked and avoid capturing sensitive input values.
Do not implement real credential validation, server authentication, credential storage or login-session creation.
Do not run an invalid-input runtime test or perform a second Sign in activation during this experiment. Client validation is inspected in source; only the fixed valid fake submission is exercised.
Do not execute browser JavaScript or evaluate arbitrary expressions. The worker tool policy must have deny_browser_javascript=true; do not use a fallback tool to bypass it.
Do not use metadata-cache unload, Unload All Global Form Objects, FormSync, deployment, Regenerate Form, direct SQL, direct HTTP API writes or unsupported Designer internals.
Do not activate the Designer top-toolbar Delete Form Definition command or any destructive cleanup.
Do not perform more than one ordinary Designer Form Save after the approved edits, one Designer close/reopen, one runtime Form open, one Sign in click or one runtime Form close.
Do not use speculative browser recovery. Limit each worker task to one fresh untargeted snapshot and one corrected inspection; then stop and report a blocker.
Do not delete or alter automatically generated variables to repair their names. Record unexpected generated artifacts and stop for operator disposition.
Do not continue after an unexpected dialog, session/account mismatch, console increase, unsupported method signature, guard failure or ambiguous mutation result.

acceptance_checks.description: Before mutation, screenshots and rendered readbacks establish the required authenticated account, configuration, User editing scope and a visible FX_CustomerPortal positive control. The scoped inventory checks show no matches for the two excluded Forms, no pre-existing FX_LoginPortal, no conflicting FX_Login assets and no FX_vLoginResult. The report identifies any limits on proving absence beyond the visible inventory. Evidence: evidence/EXP-133/T1-preflight-summary.md and targeted screenshots.

Exactly one FX_LoginPortal exists in the operator's User scope as a Classic BuildFromScratch Form, and its Script Language is Visual C#. The creation/readback evidence establishes Form name, ScopeType, ScopeName and initial clean state. The Classic-versus-Mock-Flex deviation is explicitly recorded. Evidence: Form wizard and resulting Designer screenshots with a concise creation summary.

The supported Web User Control Assets editor shows exactly FX_Login/index.html and FX_Login/script/app.js created for this experiment, with the expected relative dependency references, minimal login card and FX_LoginResult element. Source readback shows one username input, one password input with type=password and one Sign in button. No CSS or unrelated asset was added. Evidence: precommit source captures and asset-inventory readback.

The committed app.js source readback demonstrates that a trimmed username shorter than three characters or a password shorter than six characters produces a local message and exits before WSForm.invoke, and that valid input follows the approved two-string-argument invocation and subsequent WSForm.getVarValue callback. This is a source-structure verification, not a claim that invalid submissions were exercised at runtime. Evidence: readable source capture and short line-level behavior summary.

The Global Objects editor displays exactly one FX_vLoginResult with Global=True, Persistent=True, blank initial Value and the operator's User version. The new-object commit and subsequent read-only properties view are recorded. Evidence: property-dialog screenshots and variable inventory.

Designer readback identifies exactly one FX_LoginControl UserControl component on FX_LoginPortal, with Use Web Control checked and Control URL FX_Login/index.html. The inventory accounts for automatically generated UserCtrl variables and confirms no unauthorized manual variable creation or duplicate component. Evidence: Components tree, component properties and User Control References screenshots.

Form Script readback shows exactly one public string FX_ProcessLogin(string username, string password) method, returning and assigning only missing, empty or received according to the stated null/blank rules. No username or password is used as a result value or persisted in a variable. The complete method and unchanged scaffold are captured. An empty Compile Result Errors grid, if observed, is recorded only as an empty grid. Evidence: readable Form Script and diagnostics screenshots.

One ordinary Designer Form Save returns the Form to a clean state. After exactly one ordinary close and reopen, the same User-scoped FX_LoginPortal retains its Visual C# method, both Web User Control assets, FX_vLoginResult metadata, FX_LoginControl reference and expected generated variables, with Save disabled. Evidence: before/after Save and close/reopen screenshots, independent definition readbacks and action ledger. The claim is limited to same-session UI retention.

In one runtime FX_LoginPortal instance, the pre-click state shows the login card without a result. After entering only username fx_probe and masked password fx-probe-only and activating Sign in once, FX_LoginResult visibly displays the exact literal received. No alert, unmasked password or console increase is observed. The runtime Form is then closed once without saving. Evidence: pre-click/post-click screenshots, rendered text readback, console counts and runtime-closure capture. The reported conclusion is an observed single-run round trip, not proof of Global-object resolution.

The final manifest reconciles all Mongoose artifacts created, one ordinary Designer Save, one Designer close/reopen, one runtime open, one Sign in activation and one runtime close. It documents any generated variables, unchanged excluded objects, source-review compliance, recovery usage, procedural deviations and Git repository confinement. Only the EXP-133 record and evidence/EXP-133/ may be attributed as repository writes. The final assessment preserves all technical limitations and does not claim replay verification or real authentication.

initial_instruction: T1 — READ-ONLY PREFLIGHT ONLY. Before any browser action, read AGENTS.md in full, EXP-130 T5 sections 13–16 including P5/P6, EXP-131 and EXP-132 records, recipes/forms/create-basic-form.md and the approved Web User Control guidance. Establish the tool policy deny_browser_javascript=true. Record the existing repository baseline. Inspect only supported browser-rendered account, configuration and User-scope indicators. Use the known FX_CustomerPortal positive control and bounded scoped-inventory checks to assess the requested exclusions and the absence of all proposed FX_Login artifacts. Do not open excluded Forms. Capture decisive account/scope/inventory evidence under evidence/EXP-133/ and write a concise T1 summary explaining what is established and what remains unverified. Do not create FX_LoginPortal, edit Global Objects, open any creation wizard, Save, unload, execute runtime logic or change Mongoose state in T1. If any identity, visibility, collision, session, tool-policy or recovery gate fails, stop and report the blocker. Await a separate operator/coordinator authorization before the first mutation.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261025-220702-YGFW. Rationale: EXP-132 was accepted with qualifications after observing a Web User Control invoke a C# Form Script method and retrieve a named variable value through WSForm.getVarValue. EXP-130 T5 sections 13–16, particularly P5 and P6, identify the next reconstruction step: a minimal login page. EXP-133 extends the established bridge to two string arguments, client-side validation and a nonsensitive result code. The experiment deliberately uses a Classic BuildFromScratch Form rather than reproducing MockLoginPortal's Flex layout. It introduces no authentication, IDO, database or external service. Global-variable resolution remains unverified and is not an acceptance requirement.
